question.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)+{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the missing coefficients in the solution to the initial value problem, shown above.

$x(t)=$ 
{{field-1}} 
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,+$
{{field-2}}
$\,\cdot \,[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
We are told that the general solution to the system is 

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

where ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}$ are constants that are to be determined. 

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{0} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{3(0)}\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-0}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+1 \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+1=3 \\ {c}_{2}=5\end{aligned}
$$

From the first equation, we get ${c}_{1}=2.$ From the second equation, we have ${c}_{2}=5.$

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
x(t)=2\cdot [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+5\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]+{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
